title: Taking Playwright Tests From Local Runs to CI/CD
excerpt: Notes from connecting the dots between local Playwright runs and a real CI/CD pipeline built on GitHub Actions.
html:
It's a different kind of satisfaction watching your automated tests actually run in a CI/CD pipeline like GitHub Actions.

I recently spent some time exploring how this whole flow connects, from writing Playwright tests locally to running them in the cloud.

My setup is pretty simple right now. I write and run tests locally first to make sure everything works, then push changes to a develop branch. Every push triggers GitHub Actions, which runs the test suite in a clean environment.

If something breaks, I fix it locally, commit again, and push updates back to develop until everything is stable.

Once things look good, I merge develop into main using a pull request. And whenever needed, I can manually trigger full test runs using workflow_dispatch in GitHub Actions.

What I like most is this shift, from "tests running on my machine" to "tests running in a real CI pipeline." It makes everything feel more structured, reliable, and closer to how real teams work.

Overall, it was a solid hands-on experience building a production-style automated testing flow.
